modules.name: Cone registry and origin geometry
modules.design_question: Which protected views apply at a location, and where exactly are each origin, its elevation and its field of view?
modules.method: Load the City 'ViewCone' layer (EPSG:26910, 24 triangles) and cross-check it against the open-data GeoJSON (identical vertices, checked at K). Treat the first vertex of each triangle as the origin: sibling cones share it exactly (3.2.1/3.2.3/3.2.4, 9.1/9.2, B1/B2, G1/G2, J1/J2, 27.1/27.2; 3.2.2 differs by 0.33 m), giving 16 origins. The two edges leaving the apex are the vertical boundaries; the far edge near Burrard Inlet is only a clip. Read VIEWPOINT_ELEVATION_M as origin elevation Lv. Run point-in-polygon in projected metres with a 0.5 m edge tolerance, because City site sheets list points exactly on cone edges. Derive downtown and CBD subsets by intersecting wedges with a downtown box and a CBD box. Store 24 rows (id, apex, Lv, far vertices, URL, effective date), about 4 KB. Sanity checks: Lv sits within a few metres of Copernicus 90 m and City 2 m contours, so no ellipsoid mix-up.
outputs: cones.json: 24 triangles, apex = origin, Lv, far vertices; about 4 KB.
Cones touching the downtown peninsula box (computed): all except 21, 27.1, 27.2 and 28.
Cones touching the CBD core box lon -123.1255 to -123.1085, lat 49.2790 to 49.2885 (computed): 3.2.1, 3.2.2, 3.2.3, 9.1, 9.2, A, B2, D, J1.

modules.name: Lower-boundary parameter harvest and calibration
modules.design_question: What lower-boundary slope, or reference elevation and location, applies to each cone when the City publishes no height surface?
modules.method: City model (2004 sheet, 2023 bulletin, 2026 reports): each cone has origin O (X, Y, elevation Lv) and a lower boundary through a surveyed reference point (Lr, Xr, Yr). Maximum geodetic height at a site horizontal distance D from O is Z = Lv + k*D, with k = (Lr - Lv)/Dr; height above grade is Z minus base surface. The 2004 formula reproduces its worked rows to 0.01 ft. Harvest in order: (1) Council text giving a geodetic height and UTM point: Clinton Park 28, Trout Lake 27.1/27.2, H, J2; (2) 2011 reference tables for G1, H1, J1 (superseded geometry, formula checks only); (3) regression on City site sheets: A 0.05888, 3.2.3 0.000403, 9.2 0.04883; 3.2.4 copies 3.2.3 (Dec 2025); (4) for the other 16 cones request free City View Cone Assessments on a 5 by 5 grid per cone and fit k with Lv fixed. Do not derive k from named roofs alone: the 9.2 'roof of 485 W 8th Ave' test gave an implausible reference. Record provenance and status for every number.
outputs: cone_params.json: Lv, k, reference (X, Y, Lr), provenance and status per cone; about 2 KB.
Calibration table with a residual for every City value.

modules.name: Maximum-height surface engine
modules.design_question: What is the highest permitted geodetic elevation at every location, and which cone governs?
modules.method: Per cone c with wedge polygon P_c: Z_c(p) = Lv_c + k_c*|p - O_c| for p in P_c, else infinity. Surface Z(p) = min over all c, then min with zoning, Higher Buildings and aviation caps (M06). Keep an argmin raster to name the governing cone and clause. Height above ground = Z minus base surface or DEM (M04). The surface is analytic (union of circular cone sheets), so store only parameters (about 2 KB) and render rasters on demand: 2 m grid over the 4 km2 CBD is about 1 M float32 cells in a Web Worker. TIN export is optional: triangulate cone-boundary and cone-cone intersection lines densified at 5 m. Design checks are exact, not raster: clip each flat roof polygon to the wedge; worst penetration is at the roof point nearest O_c (cone is convex), so test edge-closest points, not only vertices; sloped roofs per face. Outside every polygon no view limit applies. If the City confirms axial distance, replace |p - O_c| by projection on the cone bisector.
outputs: Display raster of limit (geodetic) and argmin cone ID raster.
penetration(model) returning cone, depth in m and XYZ of worst point.
Height-above-ground raster for storey estimates.

modules.name: Vertical datum and grade conversion
modules.design_question: How do geodetic cone heights relate to terrain, building base surface and the user's model so heights compare correctly?
modules.method: The guidelines say 'geodetic' without naming a datum (s.2, p.3). City LiDAR 2022 is CGVD28GVRD (Metro Vancouver geoid) and BC legal surveys still use CGVD28 (LTSA CL 465C, 1 Apr 2026); treat cone heights as CGVD28 GVRD (assumption, flagged). Take ground from City LiDAR 2022 bare earth (0.081 m, 95%) for the CBD, falling back to the City 2013 1 m DEM. LidarBC and HRDEM use CGVD2013, about +0.15 m at Vancouver (preliminary NRCan 2013 figure): apply as a user offset. City sheets state limits against the building base surface and give geodetic = base-surface elevation + height (1070 Barclay: 178.10 - 136.72 = 41.38 m), so always compare absolute elevations, never heights over a DEM. Uploaded models: ask for the geodetic Z of one known point (competition base model datum is undocumented); store horizontal transform and dZ, displayed as model Z + dZ. Store CBD terrain as 4 m int16 centimetre tiles, about 0.5 MB raw.
outputs: terrain_cbd tiles (4 m, int16 cm).
Datum offset table and georeference dialog values.
Base-surface helper: geodetic = base + height.

modules.name: Design-versus-cone checker and clause warnings
modules.design_question: Does an uploaded model or massing break a view cone, by how much, and which guideline clause applies?
modules.method: Convert uploads (Rhino 3dm via rhino3dm, OBJ, IFC via web-ifc) to the shared frame with the M04 transform. For each cone whose wedge meets the model footprint, clip meshes and roof faces to the wedge and compute penetration p = z - Z_c at the point nearest the origin (edges and faces), including appurtenances (clause 3.1.1, printed numbering under section 3.2, p.6). Report CLEAR, BOUNDARY (within 0.1 m) or INTERSECTS, depth, XYZ and governing cone. Cite clauses: 3.1.1; 3.1.2-3.1.4 minor roof amenity encroachments (pp.6-7); 3.1.5 encroachment no more than 2 m only if hardship shown (p.7); 3.3 view shadows (p.7); 3.4 Exceptional Downtown Sites (8,000 m2 minimum; may enter QE, B1, B2, D, 12.2) and the Higher Buildings Policy. Never auto-classify minor elements, hardship or view shadows; show them as human-judgement notes. Label every result 'estimate; the City View Cone Assessment governs'.
outputs: Per-cone result: status, depth, XYZ, cone ID.
Warning list with clause number, page and quoted text.

modules.name: Other height caps: zoning, Higher Buildings, aviation
modules.design_question: Which non-view limits could lower or raise the maximum height, and are airport or harbour aviation surfaces relevant downtown?
modules.method: Zoning: the open zoning layer has no height field, so read caps from by-laws (DD sub-area A was 137.2 m in 2005; verify now). The 2023 bulletin says maps show only cone locations, and the zoning limit governs where it is lower. Higher Buildings Policy (31 Mar 2026): about 550-700 ft in the CBD, gateways about 400-515 ft; Exceptional Downtown Sites (guideline 3.4) may enter QE, B1, B2, D and 12.2. Competition towers (244-305 m) exceed those numbers, so they rely on the Exceptional route. YVR: Airport Zoning Regulations SOR/80-902 set an outer surface 45 m above an ARP assigned 2 m (about 47 m ASL) but only on Part II lands in Richmond, so downtown is not covered. No zoning regulation was found for Vancouver Harbour water aerodrome or heliport; NAV CANADA reviews case by case (Holborn 2026). Implement a user-entered aviation cap layer with a visible warning until data are obtained.
outputs: caps.json: zoning, Higher Buildings and aviation caps with source and status.
Cap layer merged into M03 minimum.

modules.name: Validation harness against City height sheets
modules.design_question: How do we prove the estimated surface matches the City's own numbers, and keep proving it as the City amends views?
modules.method: Store every City-published value as a test: 12 Robson/Cambie points, 8 Barclay values, 2004 formula rows and 2025-26 definitions. Recompute with the pipeline and fail the build when residual exceeds 0.1 m. Add a monthly job that polls the ViewCone item modified date and open-data modified date, then diffs apex, edges and EFFECTIVE_DATE. Request about 20 more City View Cone Assessments across the CBD (free; the City says 0.5-3 business days) so every downtown cone has at least 3 points, including two off-axis points to settle radial versus axial distance. Keep a record of the City sheet date and cone versions, since cones change (9.1/9.2 moved in Feb 2026; H and J2 in Dec 2025).
inputs: ViewCone item and open-data modified dates
outputs: tests/city_values.json with source, date and tolerance.

modules.name: Viewpoint camera and lower-boundary overlay
modules.design_question: How should a design be viewed from each protected origin with the cone boundaries drawn as the City draws them?
modules.method: Place the camera at origin (X, Y) with height Lv plus an eye height (not published; user parameter, default 1.6 m, team assumption). Aim along the cone bisector and set the field of view from the two boundary bearings with a margin. Draw vertical boundary lines at the two bearings. The City's overlays show the lower boundary as a straight horizontal line in a photograph (QE 3.2.3 page); for k near zero (3.2.3, 3.2.4) this equals a nearly level line, but for A (k 0.059) a straight line implies a plane tilted along the view axis rather than a circular cone. Render both candidates and compare with City reference photos before choosing. Provide rooftop viewpoints from LOD1 buildings through the same camera class. Use City photos only as links, not copies.
outputs: Camera presets per view with FOV and bearings.
Overlay of boundaries on rendered view.

flags.claim: A cone's lower boundary is a flat plane at one constant geodetic height.
flags.correction: It is a rising sight line: Z = Lv + k*D.
flags.detail: PVG wording 'horizontal lower boundary' means horizontal in the view. City 2004 formula and 12 City values fit constant k per cone: A 0.0589, 9.2 0.0488, 3.2.3 only 0.0004.

flags.claim: Vista README: origins can only be estimated from polygon geometry.
flags.correction: The polygon apex is the City's origin coordinate; sibling cones share it exactly and the City layer adds Lv.
flags.detail: 24 polygons give 16 apexes, matching the City's 16 origin points. Survey accuracy of the apex is unstated; 9.x apex are whole metres.

flags.claim: Cone heights are published nowhere, so no height test is possible.
flags.correction: No surface is published, but reference parameters appear in Council reports for several cones and the City issues per-site geodetic sheets.
flags.detail: Published or fitted now: 28, 27.1, H, J2, A, 9.2, 3.2.3, 3.2.4. The City service has empty REFERENCE_* fields for all 24.

flags.claim: YVR or harbour obstacle surfaces cap downtown heights.
flags.correction: YVR zoning (SOR/80-902) covers Richmond lands only; no zoning found for the harbour aerodrome or heliport.
flags.detail: NAV CANADA still reviews towers case by case (Holborn, July 2026: about 27 m cut); the governing surface is not public.

flags.claim: Cone 'geodetic' heights and VIEWPOINT_ELEVATION_M are CGVD28 GVRD.
flags.correction: PVG names no datum; inference from City LiDAR 2022 (CGVD28GVRD) and BC legal practice (CL 465C).
flags.detail: CGVD2013 minus CGVD28 is about +0.15 m at Vancouver (preliminary); small against the 2 m guideline tolerance but should be confirmed.
Searched PVG, Council reports, City pages, datasets. Lv matches ground within a few metres (Copernicus, contours); default 1.6 m for views is a team assumption.

flags.claim: Slope distance D is radial from the origin.
flags.correction: Radial is the 2004 formula wording; an axial (view-plane) distance is possible.
flags.detail: All 12 City sheet points lie within 4 degrees of cone axes, so radial and axial cannot be separated. An off-axis City sheet is needed.

flags.claim: A single smooth surface per cone.
flags.correction: 3.2.1 gives 123.201 m at one Barclay point but about 143.3 m at the rest.
flags.detail: Old sub-sections or stepped lower boundaries may exist (2011 report splits views into sub-cones with different reference elevations).

flags.claim: Named 'roof of building X' alignments give Lr directly.
flags.correction: The 9.2 'roof of 485 W 8th Ave' test failed.
flags.detail: Fitted k 0.0488 implies a roof about 7 m above the origin at 242 m, implausible for a mid-rise. Calibrate from City values instead.

flags.correction: Clause 3.4.2 names it, but Table 1, open data, the City layer and City pages have no 12.x view.
flags.detail: Press says 12.2 was retained and renamed; affects heights near Granville Bridge.

flags.claim: Basis of 100.58 m (330 ft) for View Cone D in 2005.
flags.correction: Report does not say if geodetic or above grade.
flags.detail: Test both readings once D is calibrated.

flags.correction: PVG Table 1 says amended 2026; Raincity says referred back.
flags.detail: Council report proposed 68.9 m for 27.2 without coordinates; service polygons seem to hold the 2026 boundaries. Confirm with City.

flags.correction: 2004 sheet gives 205 ft (62.5 m) for the old Cambie origin.
flags.detail: 2 m contours show 24-42 m near the new apex; the older figure may include something else. Confirm with City.

flags.claim: Printed reference coordinates match the named parcel corner.
flags.correction: The City's coordinates for 1975 E 12th Ave lie 76 m from the open-data parcel NE corner.
flags.detail: Use the printed UTM coordinates; treat parcel-name wording as ambiguous.

flags.claim: The PVG PDF holds the current cone definitions.
flags.correction: Council says amendments go to the GIS model and dataset and may not appear in PDF tables.
flags.detail: Treat the City layer and Council reports as authoritative; re-poll after each Council meeting.

flags.claim: Competition site may use the Exceptional Downtown Site route.
flags.correction: Site area 79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2 exceeds the 8,000 m2 minimum (3.4.1).
flags.detail: Criteria 3.4.4-3.4.8 are qualitative; the competition is hypothetical. Not a City determination.

unresolved_relationships: Reference elevation and location (Lr, Xr, Yr) for 16 cones: B1, B2, D, E, G1, G2, J1, K, 3.2.1, 3.2.2, 9.1, 10, 20, 21, 22, 27.2. Searched PVG, 2010-2026 Council reports, open data, ArcGIS layer, rezoning booklets; only roof-alignment wording found.
Eye height at origins: absent from PVG, Council reports, City pages and datasets; Lv may be ground or eye level.
Radial versus axial distance basis for the lower-boundary slope: City points lie within 4 degrees of cone axes, so cannot discriminate.
Why 3.2.1 gives 123.201 m at one Barclay point but about 143.3 m at others: sub-sections or stepped lower boundary unconfirmed.
Datum of VIEWPOINT_ELEVATION_M and cone 'geodetic' heights: PVG gives none; CGVD28 GVRD inferred.
Aviation: no public NAV CANADA or Transport Canada surfaces found for Vancouver Harbour water aerodrome, the harbour heliport or IFR procedures; searched Justice Laws, TP 1247, news.
Status of view 12.2 (Granville Bridge): cited in clause 3.4.2 but absent from Table 1, open data, City layer and City pages.
Whether view_cones.dwg carries 3D or extra attributes: only the header was read (AC1027, 14.7 KB).
Trout Lake 27.1/27.2 effective geometry and 27.2 reference coordinates after 4 Feb 2026; the 2026 Victoria Drive report was seen only as a search snippet.
Original 1989 and 2011 View Protection Guidelines per-view sheets: guidelines-view-protection.pdf redirects; Archive-It not searched.
Current CBD zoning height caps (DD sub-area A was 137.2 m in 2005) and CD-1 caps: no data layer carries height.
Vertical datum and origin of the competition Rhino base model: not stated in the brief.
Basis of the 100.58 m (330 ft) View Cone D figure in the 2005 report: geodetic or above grade.
9.x origin elevation: service 30.8 m versus 205 ft (62.5 m) in the 2004 sheet for the earlier origin.
change_log: Retry: read all 8 pages of the Public Views Guidelines PDF directly through an in-browser PDF parse; it contains no elevations, coordinates, eye height or figures.
Added: City ArcGIS 'ViewCone' layer with filled origin elevations and empty reference fields; polygon apex shown to be the origin.
Added: 2004 City formula verified on its worked rows; 12 City geodetic values fitted by a constant slope per cone.
Corrected: lower boundary is a rising sight line, not a flat plane.
Added: Council 2025-2026 numeric lower-boundary definitions (Clinton Park, Trout Lake, H, J2; 3.2.4 equals 3.2.3).
Added: aviation findings: YVR zoning excludes downtown; NAV CANADA case-by-case constraint in July 2026.
Removed: search-snippet figures (134.7 m, 166 m, 332 ft) not found in any opened document.
notes: WebFetch and curl were blocked (403); City PDFs were read via the browser's same-origin fetch and pdf.js, nothing saved. Library licences are from memory. Downtown and CBD subsets are computed, not City-published.
